title: Special issue: advanced spectroscopy in electron microscopy
content: In recent years, advances in electron microscope instrumentation and the development of diverse imaging techniques have enabled the extraction of a wide range of information beyond atomic positional data, including electric and magnetic fields. At the same time, electron irradiation of specimens induces not only inelastic scattering but also the emission of light and X rays, leading to significant progress in spectroscopic techniques that exploit these signals in a complementary manner. This special issue brings recent advances in electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), cathodoluminescence (CL) and soft X-ray emission spectroscopy (SXES), highlighting their expanding roles in probing electronic, optical and vibrational properties of materials at the nanoscale. Developments in electron optics, detection systems and data analysis now offer unprecedented access to energy, momentum and spatially resolved information, opening new frontiers in materials characterization.
